title: Love this- worth every dollar
content:
I organise walks for large groups of women, sometimes with young children and with my family and am able to find suitable walks, or even custom make walks (my new favourite thing) and guide them with confidence. The maps are downloadable so you can use them in aeroplane mode and save battery. Cross sections provide a good overview for walkers. Reviews help when tracks have been closed or in need of repair or that are hard to find. It is even able to alert you should you miss a turn. 
I’ve also been fortunate enough to have travelled the world and am able to use this in every country I’ve been. I can’t rate this enough. I love trawling over map locations, reading reviews, looking at photos and searching for the next perfect walk. 
If you need a good map companion download to your phone- this is the app for you.

title: Awesome App for Adventuring
content:
The community is amazing. There’s strong collaboration across the platform to share experiences and gorgeous locations that you otherwise can’t find on your traditional Google or Apple maps. 

I personally appreciated the fact that it has the three grades of Easy, Intermediate and Hard. I like to use my hikes to fly out my drone (DJI Air 3) so I typically find myself on solo hikes - so starting with Easy and phasing into Intermediate/Hard over time really helped build my confidence. It’s definitely beginner friendly and helps you build your skills out there. 

The downloadable maps are the game-changer (not sure if it’s a premium feature 🫣) but being able to use maps in low reception areas has unlocked so much opportunity to keep going without concern for getting lost. 

10/10 would recommend.

Biggest piece of advice for newbies: start easy and build from there. Even for intermediate hikers - some of the intermediate hikes on the platform can be sitting between intermediate and hard so would recommend reading the reviews in advance and planning appropriately. Other than that, happy exploring!

- Trail Discovery: Easily find new trails and explore different areas.
- Reviews and Ratings: Get valuable insights from other hikers to help plan your trip.
- Maps and Navigation: Stay on track with detailed maps and GPS navigation.
- Offline Access: Access trail maps and information even without cell service.

My only suggestion for improvement would be to add more trail updates and maintenance information.

Overall, AllTrails is a fantastic resource for hikers of all levels. Whether you're a seasoned pro or just starting out, this app is a must-have for planning and navigating your next adventure.

title: Awesome App for Adventuring
content:
The community is amazing. There’s strong collaboration across the platform to share experiences and gorgeous locations that you otherwise can’t find on your traditional Google or Apple maps. 

I personally appreciated the fact that it has the three grades of Easy, Intermediate and Hard. I like to use my hikes to fly out my drone (DJI Air 3) so I typically find myself on solo hikes - so starting with Easy and phasing into Intermediate/Hard over time really helped build my confidence. It’s definitely beginner friendly and helps you build your skills out there. 

The downloadable maps are the game-changer (not sure if it’s a premium feature 🫣) but being able to use maps in low reception areas has unlocked so much opportunity to keep going without concern for getting lost. 

10/10 would recommend.

Biggest piece of advice for newbies: start easy and build from there. Even for intermediate hikers - some of the intermediate hikes on the platform can be sitting between intermediate and hard so would recommend reading the reviews in advance and planning appropriately. Other than that, happy exploring!

content:
AllTrails Review: A Hiker's Best Friend

I've been using AllTrails for a while now, and it's become an essential part of my hiking routine. The app offers a vast database of trails, complete with reviews, ratings, and detailed maps.

The features I love most about AllTrails include:

- Trail Discovery: Easily find new trails and explore different areas.
- Reviews and Ratings: Get valuable insights from other hikers to help plan your trip.
- Maps and Navigation: Stay on track with detailed maps and GPS navigation.
- Offline Access: Access trail maps and information even without cell service.

My only suggestion for improvement would be to add more trail updates and maintenance information.

Overall, AllTrails is a fantastic resource for hikers of all levels. Whether you're a seasoned pro or just starting out, this app is a must-have for planning and navigating your next adventure.

content:
Love love love this app! It’s probably the only walking app you really need. And you can use if for so much more than you initially think. The app even contains a handy ‘lifeline’ feature where you can share your activity with contacts in case something goes wrong and you have to be found. 

You’re able to access the activities you have tracked or your reviews with photos as a history under your profile which is nice. It would be great if you could search them somehow by area etc. 

The only negatives are that the user xp is occasionally a little unintuitive at first although I have noticed some improvements over time. I would love to be able to go back to edit my stored trail data, for instance if I forgot to turn off the tracking when I finished the trail. title: Great app but frustrating at times.
content:
I’ve used this app for the last 2 years, on short hikes and multi day hikes all over the east coast of Australia and a bit of Patagonia. I couldn’t fault the maps they seem to always be up to date and have not failed me yet. It’s the best app for hiking that I know of so I’d recommend it for sure. 

While the offline tracking mode is accurate and consistent it consumes far too much battery for a multi day hike. Which isn’t a big problem you just don’t track the hike and use the map freely. 

Only it doesn’t really work that well with out the tracking function. Every time I boot the app to check my location, it shoots me way out of my direct spot to the overview of the entire walk or in some cases the entire country. And I have to then manually zoom in to relocate my position. It’s a relatively small issue but it’s pretty annoying after a couple of years of consistence use. Honestly I’d rather not use the tracking function but like a digital map but it seems to prioritise an athlete tracking performance rather than someone hiking for leisure. 

Also you’re forced to rate hikes after completion. I don’t wanna rate hikes, rating hikes is almost as lame as ratings apps. So I have to force quit the app to circumvent it. 

Apart from that it’s great app and I’ll update my review to 5 stars if they ever fix it.

title: Great app but frustrating at times.
content:
I’ve used this app for the last 2 years, on short hikes and multi day hikes all over the east coast of Australia and a bit of Patagonia. I couldn’t fault the maps they seem to always be up to date and have not failed me yet. It’s the best app for hiking that I know of so I’d recommend it for sure. 

While the offline tracking mode is accurate and consistent it consumes far too much battery for a multi day hike. Which isn’t a big problem you just don’t track the hike and use the map freely. 

Only it doesn’t really work that well with out the tracking function. Every time I boot the app to check my location, it shoots me way out of my direct spot to the overview of the entire walk or in some cases the entire country. And I have to then manually zoom in to relocate my position. It’s a relatively small issue but it’s pretty annoying after a couple of years of consistence use. Honestly I’d rather not use the tracking function but like a digital map but it seems to prioritise an athlete tracking performance rather than someone hiking for leisure. 

Also you’re forced to rate hikes after completion. I don’t wanna rate hikes, rating hikes is almost as lame as ratings apps. So I have to force quit the app to circumvent it. 

Apart from that it’s great app and I’ll update my review to 5 stars if they ever fix it.
